title: Sapphire Lane Dashboard — contextual payload lanes & retry choreography
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: SREs and product engineers currently spend too long stitching together logs, traces, and payloads to understand why inference requests fail or retry. Existing console flows surface single-request details but not the ‘lane’ — the contextual sequence of upstream transforms, KV-cache interactions, and automatic retry choreography that led to the failure.

Goal: Design a compact, scannable dashboard panel — “Sapphire Lane” — that groups related failed requests into contextual lanes, shows retry chains, highlights suspicious payload diffs, and exposes quick replay / canary controls for operators. The panel should reduce median time-to-root-cause (MTTR) for inference errors and provide safe, auditable quick-actions for retries and rollbacks.

Users: On-call SREs, ML infra engineers, platform reliability leads, and debugging-oriented PMs.

Key constraints: must fit into existing Console row layout (per-route dashboards), be performant with >1000 related events, not leak PII by default (payload redaction rules), obey RBAC for replay actions, and integrate with runtime-1.20 tracing headers.

Design pillars: 
- Scannability: compact summary rows with inline taxonomy badges and deviation fingerprints.
- Contextuality: group by causal chain (origin request, retries, fallbacks) and display the most relevant payload diff.
- Safety: require two-step confirmation + audit log for manual replays; surface risk level for automated retry suggestions.
- Instrumentation-first: every lane includes links to token-level cost delta and KV cache hit/miss stats.

Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma prototype with keyboard navigation, a short PRD summarizing acceptance criteria, an annotated accessibility pass, and a review doc for ENG/PM to estimate backend work for grouping and pagination.

Design assumptions (to validate): grouping heuristics can be computed from existing trace IDs + request fingerprint; payload diffing within first 1KB yields useful signals; privacy-sensitive payloads flagged by heuristics can be shown only to users with appropriate access.

Out of scope: full time-travel replay; multi-region cross-tenant correlation (follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Visual: Prototype renders within Console route-detail panel at 1200px width and matches provided Figma frames
Grouping: Related requests (same fingerprint or causal trace) are collapsed into a single lane with expandable timeline
Payload: Payload diff highlights first-party keys and redacts values matching PII rules by default
Actions: Replay and rerun buttons trigger modal with role-gated confirmation and create audit log entries
Performance: Panel loads within 600ms for groups up to 1,000 events using paginated fetches
Metrics: Shortlink created to link lanes to existing SLO dashboards; MTTR baseline and improvement target defined in PRD

open_questions: Which exact heuristics should be server-side vs client-side for lane grouping?
What redaction heuristics do we inherit from the logs team and can we reuse them?
Do we allow one-click replay on low-risk retries or require explicit canary selection?
Should the diff strip include model inputs-only or both inputs+metadata by default?
